The West Side Story star welcomes her friends’ jokes, saying they can do whatever they want
Rita Moreno will soon celebrate turning 95 — and she’s doing it with her signature sense of humor.
At the Día De Muertos Gala at the Universal Studios Backlot in Universal City, Calif., the 94-year-old actress opened up about plans for her birthday, which is on Dec. 11.
Asked how she will celebrate the occasion, she said she plans to have dinner with close friends, but with a slight twist.
The West Side Story actress told E! she intends to allow her close pals to have a bit of playful fun at her expense.
“We’re gonna have a dinner and, you know, I’m sure people will be insulting me all night,” she added.
When asked if that meant it would be a roast, Moreno answered, “Absolutely. Why not?”

“They can do whatever they damn want,” she added. “It’s just a wonderful way to celebrate, so I can’t wait.”
Moreno, an actress, singer, and dancer , has an impressive career that spans more than 70 years.
She’s starred in a slew of iconic musicals — including Singin’ in the Rain , The King and I , the original 1961 West Side Story film and Steven Spielberg’s remake — and is one of the few stars in Hollywood to have earned the prestigious EGOT (an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar and a Tony).
